segments.t: In her small Parisian apartment, Camille Valentini has a hurried breakfast with her visiting mother, Annick. While Annick comments on celebrity hairstyles and asks about Camille's relationship with Mathias, Camille tries not to be late for work. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Tu ne prends pas de petit-déjeuner?
Maman, je suis très en retard.
Assieds-toi et mange un peu.
Qui coiffe cette pauvre actrice?
Les agents ne s'occupent pas des coiffures.
Dis-moi, Mathias est gentil avec toi?
Oui, il est bien plus gentil qu'avant.
On se voit et on déjeune ensemble.
Regarde, il m'a offert une jolie lampe.
C'est facile quand on est très riche.
J'allume ta belle bougie tous les soirs.
J'aurais dû garder un enfant à la maison.
Tu as un vrai don pour le drame.
Fais bien attention sur ton vélo.
Let's examine how Annick and Camille discuss family and work over breakfast.
Tu ne prends pas de petit-déjeuner?
'Are you not having breakfast?' Annick opens with the word for 'have' and lands on 'morning meal' at the close.
Maman, je suis très en retard.
'Mom, I am very late.' An adverb of degree emphasizing time pressure.
Assieds-toi et mange un peu.
'Sit down and eat a little.' A coordinated pair of imperative verbs.
Qui coiffe cette pauvre actrice?
'Who styles this poor actress's hair?' An interrogative pronoun followed by a critical remark.
Les agents ne s'occupent pas des coiffures.
'Agents do not deal with hairstyles.' A pronominal verb defining professional scope.
Dis-moi, Mathias est gentil avec toi?
'Tell me, is Mathias nice to you?' Annick gives a direct imperative using the verb for 'tell me'.
Oui, il est bien plus gentil qu'avant.
'Yes, he is much nicer than before.' A comparative adverb construction showing improvement.
On se voit et on déjeune ensemble.
'We see each other and have lunch together.' Reciprocal pronominal actions in informal speech.
Regarde, il m'a offert une jolie lampe.
'Look, he gave me a pretty lamp.' A compound past verb showing a thoughtful gift.
C'est facile quand on est très riche.
'It is easy when one is very rich.' The adverb meaning 'very' sharpens the verb for 'is' here.
J'allume ta belle bougie tous les soirs.
'I light your lovely candle every evening.' A temporal routine phrase reassuring her mother.
J'aurais dû garder un enfant à la maison.
'I should have kept a child at home.' A past conditional expressing nostalgic maternal longing.
Tu as un vrai don pour le drame.
'You have a real gift for drama.' Camille opens with the word for 'have' and lands on 'theatrical drama' at the close.
Fais bien attention sur ton vélo.
'Be very careful on your bicycle.' Listen for the expression meaning 'pay', which leads naturally into 'bicycle'. Now let's listen to Camille and Annick's morning conversation again at full speed.

Annick's visit reminds Camille of her complicated family situation, as Mathias remains her secret father. Despite the maternal guilt, Camille hurries out the door to face another busy day at the agency. We'll pick up right after this in the next scene.
À ce soir, maman!
